commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
Preserve task-owned shell tools across curation and rollouts (#10029)

TaskSpecs can bind a declared interaction tool to Bash execution,
preserving the tool name, argument schema and prompt across curation and
rollout. A task declaring Bash(script) keeps that interface even when
the harness prefers terminal(cmd). Tasks declaring only a shell
capability use the harness interface, which defaults to shell(command).

Curation and RolloutEngine share command decoding and Bash execution.
The built-in session supports one shell binding per task with one
required, unconstrained string argument. Unsupported schemas, unbound
interaction tools and name collisions fail before machine acquisition.
Tool names alone do not select execution behavior.

TaskSpec schema advances to 0.27; older TaskSpec records must be
regenerated from their source data. The QUICK output version advances to
regenerate TaskSpecs while reusing downloaded sources. Rollout shell
observations now use separate stdout_truncated and stderr_truncated
fields in place of the combined truncated field.

---------

Co-authored-by: rjpower <rjpower@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
Separate task requirements from Shellbox execution (#10021)

Separate task requirements from machine selection. TaskSpec schema 0.26
declares agent and grader software plus `LINUX_PROCESS` or
`SHELL_SIMULATOR` semantics. Curation controls and RolloutEngine share
validation and preparation, preserving required variables, working
directories and setup commands. Dependency lockfiles currently require
the Local bubblewrap backend; memory limits there are advisory. Unbuilt
image recipes and incompatible machines fail before machine creation.
Oracle controls use the agent's requirements, falling back to the grader
environment only when those requirements are empty.

The campaign supplies Shellbox factories. Image graders can use gVisor
through Iris or Daytona; remove the host-Docker worker path, which
ordinary Kubernetes workers cannot provide. These deployment choices
stay outside TaskSpec.

Use `output_paths` for submission files and recursive directory roots.
Shellbox owns bounded transfer; the runtime collects the declared
submission for isolated grading. TaskTrove Python task datasets declare
`/app` without inferring filenames from prompts or hidden tests. Their
instructions remain unchanged. Shared Harbor workspaces require no
transfer; isolated Harbor exports declare file or directory artifacts.
Episode and rollout execution expose the same runtime-provided
`shell(command)` tool, executing commands with `bash -c`.

Move TaskTrove conversion and Harbor export into the curation
experiment. The exporter preserves legacy pytest image construction,
including dependency checks used only for those images. Delete the
obsolete Clean TaskTrove importer, duplicate capture schema and unused
conversion metadata.

Replace automatic Python source hashing with explicit recipe, stage,
control and export versions. Changes to converters, bundled graders or
pipeline behavior require a bump to the corresponding version. Data and
artifact integrity hashes remain. Advance the affected output versions
while preserving download versions; older TaskSpec Parquet must be
reconverted.

Co-authored-by: rjpower <rjpower@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: yonromai
commits.message:
Share Hero and Snowball checkpoint export mechanics

Share bounded HF shard-writing code between Hero and the Levanter converter used by Snowball. Hero reuses the converter's 5 GB file planner; a source tensor larger than that target remains whole. Local files are written directly, while remote files stage under `TMPDIR` before upload.

All JAX ranks replicate tensors in matching order. Only process zero copies weights to CPU and writes files. One writer process supports host-local paths and existing HF upload callbacks. An `ExitStack` owns each memory reservation during gathering; successful submission transfers cleanup to the shard-write task's completion callback. Process zero broadcasts writer failures at matching checks on all ranks.

Hero resume verifies the export request identity and shard checksums before reuse. It writes `export-manifest.json` after all shards and HF metadata to mark completion.

CPU export checks cover exact Hero/Snowball weights, concurrent uploads and two-rank failure/recovery. Full-size accelerator exports and live cloud/HF uploads remain untested.

commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
[dependencies] Publish RL libraries as Marin packages (#9982)

Publish Verifyit, TaskCompendium, and RolloutEngine as `marin-*`
distributions in the coupled Python release. Their wheels pin Marin
sibling dependencies to the same release version. Verifyit's `math`
extra installs symbolic grading dependencies; its base package covers
exact and numeric grading.

Shellbox and RolloutEngine now use the root uv workspace like the other
released Python libraries. RolloutEngine's separate lock and unused
Harbor task importer are removed. Verifyit, the TaskTrove grader image,
and the root lock no longer require the separate `harbor-config`
package. The wheel builder and publishing guide use the release registry
as their package list.

The TaskTrove exporter now emits Harbor TOML without importing Harbor.
It records that per-task schema validation has not run; a representative
export passed the pinned isolated Harbor runtime's schema check. Local
validation built all twelve wheels and source archives through the
release entry point. The safe suite passed 2,723 tests; the
TaskCompendium, RolloutEngine, and Shellbox lanes, strict docs build,
and type check passed. The MarinSkyRL manifest migration is prepared on
[its work
branch](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/tree/agent/20261009-pypi-marin-deps);
its lock can be refreshed after this release publishes the new
distributions.

Part of #9929

commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
[rl-data] Parse SWE-rebench Elixir trace records (#10008)

Normalize ExUnit's leading `*` trace marker before the archived
SWE-rebench Elixir parser sees test output. The parser expects `test ...
(...)`; with the reported `* test ... (0.1ms) [L#528]`, it returns no
named statuses and scores a passing oracle as zero after #9970 removed
the exit-code fallback.

The emitted verifier resolves named passing records and leaves a failing
record unresolved. The task-curation suite passed on this branch (474
passed, 9 skipped). The broader safe suite passed before the branch was
rebased onto merged main (2,928 passed, 12 skipped, 5 expected
failures). The archived Harbor oracle was not rerun locally.

Fixes #10003

[task-curation] Remove redundant tests and unused fixtures (#10018)

Remove catalog-wide type and configuration checks, duplicate round-trip
and scorer runs, and redundant parameter combinations. Delete fixtures
used only by those tests. Keep behavioral coverage for grading, privacy,

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
Let each RL source define its curation pipeline (#10015)

Each `RlDataSource` pairs typed dataset configuration with a plain
`pipeline(source, options)` callable returning an artifact graph.
Pipelines choose ingestion and optional stages. `process_rows` provides
the existing row conversion, review and control workflow for reuse.

QUICK executes the declared graph locally, reuses pinned downloads and
accepts staged inputs. The row processor skips review and grading in
QUICK, and requires model settings only when a rubric is configured.
Results report named outputs and executed stages. Atlas reads catalog
facts from configuration; grader builds use explicit environment
registration.

Registration edits change converter file hashes and the calendar golden
module hash, causing a one-time change to reviewed artifact addresses.
Download identities, `PIPELINE_VERSION` and the generated Atlas catalog
remain unchanged; stored artifacts are retained.

---------

Co-authored-by: rjpower <rjpower@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[rl] Return task review evidence through pipeline sinks (#10017)

Expose review_tasks for direct TaskSpec batch review, returning reviews
and structured request, response, retry, and cache observations. Zephyr
sinks write one evidence record per batch alongside the existing audit
rows in one execution.

Evidence now uses batch records in Parquet instead of attempt
directories. The persistent request cache, request identities, retries,
and task eligibility are preserved. Handled provider failures remain in
returned observations. Evidence is committed by the sink; unexpected
worker failures propagate with no guarantee of evidence durability.

Co-authored-by: rjpower <rjpower@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[rl-data] Reuse conversion with dataset-owned ingestion (#10016)

Allow dataset-owned ingestion to reuse task conversion and Parquet
output without constructing a SourceRecipe. Converted rows carry tasks
or typed rejections while retaining caller-supplied identity, resources
and rewrites. Output writing produces conversion shards and an
unreviewed manifest, returning paths and row counts with optional
execution telemetry. The existing QUICK path uses the same helpers while
preserving its decoding provenance, source metadata and output policy.

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[iris] Renew worker credentials before expiry (#10010)

Renew worker credentials one day before their 30-day expiry, including
while workers are idle, and persist replacements across process
restarts. Restrict renewal to authenticated workers and admins; expired
credentials still require operator recovery. Controllers refresh
provisioning credentials, and manual worker creation and restart obtain
fresh tokens from the controller.

An expired worker token could remain unnoticed while the log client
reused a cached Finelog endpoint. After a timeout invalidated that
cache, controller endpoint discovery rejected the token and log batches
were discarded even though tasks continued running. The October 9 audit
found expired credentials on six CPU workers; targeted credential
replacement and process restarts restored central logging without
restarting their seven task containers.

Deploy the controller renewal RPC before the worker changes. Worker
tokens remain shared identities without individual revocation; a stolen
token can also renew itself.

[Incident diagnosis and recovery](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/691).

---------
